newsitem.title: FRANCE: Wheat quality fears rise in centre-west France.
newsitem.headline: Wheat quality fears rise in centre-west France.

text.p: The wheat harvest is expected to start over the weekend in Poitou-Charentes in centre-west France but there are already signs that rain in June led to unwanted germination in the fields, crop analysts said on Thursday.
"There is some serious concern. Initial tests show evidence of germination, which should hurt quality," a crop analyst for the local ONIC grain office in Poitiers said.
Experts said it was premature to estimate the extent of the damage but coastal areas suffered less than the hinterland because the wheat there matured less quickly.
Rain throughout June also stopped the rapeseed harvest in its tracks and delayed the start of the barley and wheat harvest by some 10 days.
Last weekend the return of dry weather conditions allowed farmers to resume rapeseed cuts and start harvesting barley.
Substantial rain in May and June helped rapeseed crops recover after nearly four months of drought but soft wheat and barley yields should be hit, analysts said.
"Good weather conditions in May did not offset the losses caused by the March-April drought," one analyst said.
Local ONIC officials now predict regional soft wheat yields may fall to 5.5 tonnes per hectare from 6.1 tonnes last year.
Barley yields may drop to five tonnes from a record six tonnes in 1996.
Dry conditions in the spring also raised barley protein content in some areas above the 11 percent required by the malt industry, analysts said.
Officials said they had revised upwards their estimates for the regional rapeseed yield to 3.2-3.5 tonnes from a previous forecast of three tonnes. Last year's yield was 3.5 tonnes.
Regional sowings are set to rise by 4.8 pct to 372,000 hectares for soft wheat, by 11.6 percent to 99,000 hectares for barley and by over 37 percent to 86,500 hectares for rapeseed.
